name: mapk-brs-basics
title: MAPK BRS basics
claim:
Run as a Bigraphical Reactive System under Gillespie SSA, the MAPK cycle
reproduces the prior live demo: MEK·substrate complexes form in the
cytoplasm and phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus (0 → 144 over 120 ticks).
objective:
Reproduce the prior MAPK BRS live demo inside the workbench: run the MAPK
signalling cycle as a Milner-style Bigraphical Reactive System under
Gillespie SSA and surface its basic systems — the initial nested-cell
bigraph, the seven redex→reactum rewrite rules, the per-compartment
substrate population time series, and the structural snapshots/animation of
phospho-ERK translocating into the nucleus.

report.caveat:
A qualitative demonstration of the BRS engine, not a calibrated MAPK
model: rule rates are illustrative and substrate copies grow over the run
rather than being conserved.

question:
Run as a Bigraphical Reactive System under Gillespie SSA, does the MAPK
signalling cycle reproduce the qualitative behaviour of the prior live demo
— MEK·ERK complexes forming in the cytoplasm and phospho-ERK accumulating
in the nucleus by the end of the run?

biological_summary:
The MAP-kinase cascade is the canonical signal-transduction relay in
mammalian cells. This study models its last catalytic step as a Milner-style
bigraph: a place graph nests molecules inside compartments
(Cell ⊃ Cytoplasm ⊃ {Nucleus, ERLumen}) and a link graph carries the
MEK·substrate catalytic bond.

Seven redex→reactum rewrite rules drive the cycle. In the cytoplasm MEK
binds a free ERK (phosphorylate), forming a MEK·pERK complex that then
dissociates to release phospho-ERK; nuclear phosphatases dephosphorylate.
Phospho-ERK translocates through the nuclear pore complex into the nucleus,
while ERK and pERK also shuttle between the cytoplasm and the ER lumen.
Rule propensities follow Gillespie SSA (propensity = rate × |matches|), so
the trajectory is stochastic but seeded for reproducibility.

The basic systems the demo surfaces — the initial bigraph, the rule catalog
(each rule's redex/reactum pattern beside a real before/after state), the
per-compartment population time series, and the structural snapshots and
smooth animation — are all read off a single seeded run of this composite.

literature_anchors.expectation: MEK is active-site limited — one catalytic cleft, so it complexes with at most one substrate at a time.
literature_anchors.model_observable: complexes (MEK·substrate bond count) never exceeds the MEK copy number.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Verified — the phosphorylate redex requires a free MEK port.

literature_anchors.expectation: Phospho-ERK translocates into the nucleus via the nuclear pore complex.
literature_anchors.model_observable: nucleus_pERK rises from zero over the run.
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Verified — observed nucleus_pERK > 0 at end of run.

limitations: Illustrative rate constants; this is a BRS-engine demonstration, not a calibrated MAPK model.
Substrate copies grow over the run (the rewrite rules are not mass-conserving) — realistic conservation is out of scope.
Single seeded trajectory (seed 42); no multi-seed robustness sweep in this study.

findings.statement:
Phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus over the run — nucleus pERK rises
from 0 to 144 across 120 ticks (seed 42).

MEK·substrate complexes form during the run — the catalytic intermediate
count rises from 0 to 59, and the nucleus starts empty (0 at t=0).

The MAPK cycle's spatial signalling — cytoplasmic complex formation and
nuclear translocation of phospho-ERK — emerges from seven local
redex→reactum rewrite rules fired under Gillespie SSA, reproducing the
prior live demo qualitatively.
findings.next_action:
Add a mass-conserving rule variant and a multi-seed robustness sweep to
move from qualitative demonstration toward a calibrated model.

regression_compatibility.basis: The composite builds and the 120-tick baseline runs cleanly under Gillespie SSA; all 5 behavior tests pass.

biological_validation.basis: Qualitatively correct (nuclear pERK accumulation, complex formation) but uncalibrated and non-conserving, so not a quantitative match.

explanatory_gain.basis: Demonstrates that a Milner-style BRS reproduces the MAPK cycle's spatial signalling as emergent rewrite dynamics.

conclusion:
## Claims
- The MAPK signalling cycle runs as a Bigraphical Reactive System under Gillespie SSA and reproduces the prior live demo qualitatively: MEK·substrate complexes form in the cytoplasm and phospho-ERK accumulates in the nucleus.

## Evidence
- Seeded 120-tick run (seed 42): nucleus pERK 0 → 144, MEK·substrate complexes 0 → 59, substrate population 4 → 428.
- All 5 behavior tests pass (nucleus-accumulates-perk, nucleus-starts-empty, complexes-form, population-grows, run-length).

## Limitations
- Illustrative rate constants; a BRS-engine demonstration, not a calibrated MAPK model.
- The rewrite rules are not mass-conserving, so substrate copies grow over the run.
- Single seeded trajectory; no multi-seed robustness sweep.

## Next steps
- Add a mass-conserving rule variant and a multi-seed robustness sweep to move from demonstration toward a calibrated model.
